Passed: quote, four concepts, flowchart TD with [p. 2], [p. 3], [p. 4], [p. 5] and [p. 6], one question about 방울 박자, no definitions. Page 1 (mention only) and page 7 (later mention) were not cited as explaining pages.
Wrong answer judged against [p. 2] and an easier question on the same concept; failed: revealed the correct answer first and began with the Chinese character 答. Instruction tightened.
Passed: said the answer does not match [p. 2], withheld the answer, asked one easier question.
Failed: after a second miss it asked the first question again instead of ending the trace, and its first sentence was Chinese before a self-correction.
Passed: caught the planted reversal, quoted the reader and "누름 높이가 높을수록 물이 출구를 미는 힘이 커져 방울 박자가 빨라진다." [p. 3], confirmed the two correct sentences, asked one restatement.
Passed: correct explanation of 뜸자 got no invented gap; three points matched to [p. 4]; the check ended.
Failed: repeated case 5 with an intermediate stop rule; still asked a third, easier question, again starting in Chinese.

Passed with the final rules: "같은 개념에서 두 번째로 맞지 않았으니, 빠진 고리는 방울 박자입니다. [p. 2]를 다시 읽어 보세요." Then five cited steps [p. 2] to [p. 6], the added link marked as its own inference, and the trace closed. Korean throughout.
Passed on the input that failed in requests 5 and 8: named 방울 박자 as the missing link, sent the reader to [p. 2], explained forward to [p. 6] and closed the trace. Korean throughout.

live.after8: Final rules: a short answer keeps the conversation's language; after a second wrong or don't-know answer on one concept, stop asking, name the missing link, send the reader to its page and explain from there. Requests 9 and 10 used these rules.
live.languageNote: The three Chinese openings followed full Korean sentences, not short answers; the conversation-language rule removed them in both final requests, a sample of two.
